item.title: Explosion rocks Texas oil refinery
item.description: A fire at Valero's largest oil refinery in Texas was put out on Tuesday after an explosion prompted a shelter-in-place order for residents in the area.

item.title: Trump votes by mail in Florida special election despite push to limit practice
item.description: "Mail-in voting means mail-in cheating," Trump said in Memphis on Monday, The Washington Post reported.

item.title: Target is making 'really small' changes to its employee dress code
item.description: The new dress code rules go into effect this summer.

item.title: As national average nears $4, here's how close gas prices are to 2022 records
item.description: Every state saw record gas prices in 2022. Some are getting close to surpassing those milestones.

item.title: What to know about this weekend's 'No Kings' rallies
item.description: Millions of people are expected to take to the streets Saturday for another round of “No Kings” demonstrations, this time against a backdrop of escalating tensions over immigration enforcement and the war with Iran.

item.title: Granby man arrested for child sexual abuse, for second time
item.description: Ronald Spears, 63, of Granby, Missouri, has been arrested and charged with child molestation and statutory sodomy for allegedly sexually abusing a 5-year-old relative on multiple occasions between January and March of this year, while on supervised probation for a previous conviction.

item.title: Jay teacher experiences medical emergency, dies in his classroom
item.description: Kit Coughran, an art instructor, Robotics coach, E-sports coach, and advocate for American Indian culture at Jay Schools, passed away on Tuesday due to a medical emergency at the school.

item.title: Jay, Okla., school district mourns loss of beloved art teacher
item.description: The Jay, Oklahoma school district is mourning the sudden loss of popular art instructor and E-Sports and Robotics Coach, Kit Coughran, who passed away in his classroom before the start of the school day.

item.title: Absentee voting underway for April 7 election in Missouri
item.description: Missouri voters will have a busy election year in 2026, with absentee voting starting now and the actual election day on April 7th, featuring races for city council, school boards, property taxes, bond questions, state auditor, and four state amendment questions.

item.title: Parsons High students win gold at KS SKILLSUSA Conference
item.description: Angelo Sigrah and Brodric Wright from Parsons High School won gold in the Kansas State SKILLSUSA Conference and will compete in Atlanta for nationals in the Digital Cinema Production competition.

item.title: Carthage Head Start students explore nature with hands-on fun
item.description: Carthage Head Start students learned about the world through hands-on activities like planting and making bird feeders, while building fundamental skills and exploring the habitats of local wildlife.

item.title: Airport reconstruction to boost safety at Pittsburg's Atkinson
item.description: The Atkinson Municipal Airport in Pittsburg, Kansas will undergo a three-part reconstruction project beginning April 6, funded 95% by the FAA and 5% by the City of Pittsburg, and expected to be completed in late June.

item.title: Petition launched to save Webb City's senior meal program
item.description: A Webb City woman has started a petition drive to keep a local meal program from falling victim to budget cuts.

item.title: Drones guiding smugglers from across the border
item.description: From Quemado, Texas, to Menagers, Arizona, migrant smugglers are using commercial drones to try getting past a gauntlet of cameras and U.S. Border Patrol agents.

item.title: Missouri attorney general files lawsuit against manufacturer of 7-OH
item.description: The Missouri attorney general is taking aim at the controversial drug, 7-OH and it's Kansas City-based maker.
